- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline at 5–10% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 7–14 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early period (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or 1.00 extremes, model may be overfitting; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
